cells.tense: The whole structure stands finished and you're still here with the pen.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're carrying that's already done, and set it down where the next person can pick it up.
cells.core:
You finish things, and you know you finish them. Not everything you start, but the ones that matter — you see them through the middle stretch where nothing visible is changing, and you're here at the other end with the thing standing. What it took, you paid. It's something you do, and you do it without much ceremony, which is why people lean on you and why so few of them say it out loud.

What's alive here is the clearing — the part where what's done gets set down so what's next has somewhere to stand. You're good at the building and quieter about the putting-down. The strength isn't holding harder. It's holding what's real without gripping what's over. So name one finished thing and put it down in the open, out loud, once.
cells.sheetLine: You finish what matters. Now finish the putting-down too.
cells.verb: completing a sustained effort and closing the cycle
cells.place: at a threshold where something old has to fully end

cells.tense: You're living past the ending, rehearsing how it should land.
cells.ask: Pick one decision you've already made and stop explaining it to anyone for a week. Let it stand on the doing.
cells.core:
You can see the ending from here, and you want it handled right. So you're pushing the close ahead of where it actually is — the loose ends, the last conversation, the thing that hasn't finished finishing — and every push makes the ending later. The work is done or nearly done. What's running is you, adding one more coat of paint where the wall was already dry.

What's needed here isn't more holding-together. It's you letting something be finished without signing off on it three more times. Nothing lands until it's allowed to be over. So pick one decision that's already made, keep it, and let the doing speak instead of the explaining.
cells.sheetLine: The ending isn't late. You're just ahead of it.

cells.tense: You're on the near side of a finishing and still holding what it left.
cells.ask: Take one object off your desk or out of your bag that belongs to something already over, and put it somewhere you won't see it daily.
cells.core:
You're still holding what a finished thing left behind. Not stuck exactly — still carrying. The evidence is in small things: a stack you haven't cleared, a name you say carefully, a route you don't take anymore because it goes past something. The finishing happened. The standing-in-it didn't.

This isn't a failure of will. You can build. What's missing is the last move of the cycle — looking at where you actually are now, with the thing behind you, and letting that be the view. Seeing clearly comes first, and it doesn't require you to announce anything or feel any particular way about what ended. Take one object from that old thing and put it out of daily sight.
cells.sheetLine: The work is over. You're still carrying it around.
cells.verb: completing a sustained effort and closing the cycle
cells.place: at a threshold where something old has to fully end

cells.tense: You're finishing something right now and calling it just how things went.
cells.ask: Say 'I'm the one ending this' about one thing already winding down, to one person, without softening it.
cells.core:
Something is closing in your life right now and you're describing it as if it wound down on its own — it came, it went, that's how it goes. What's actually happening is you. You're the one making the calls that end it, keeping the pace, choosing what stays and what's left behind. The pen's in your hand and you're pointing at the door like someone else walked through it.

Claiming the ending isn't arrogance. It's just accuracy — and accuracy is the whole tool here, seeing the thing as it is before you decide what to do with it. So far you've been seeing it as something that happened to you. Say out loud, once, to one person, that you're the one ending this.
cells.sheetLine: It didn't wind down on its own. You wound it down.
